'''Rust, Sword and the Sun''' is a Segue in [[Chapter II]] of the [[Main Quests|Main Quest]].

==Summary==
You and Abby arrive at Solis Tavern. While waiting for contact from the Ephor's Palace, you run into a blind wandering bard, Nestor. He shares with you Augusta's stories before she rose to power.

A girl whose homeland was devastated by the Dark Tide, Augusta, follows Septimont's Gladiators to the city. Her heart yearns to find the power to protect her home, and the crowd's buzz of the Great Agon catches her attention. The girl thinks this path may help her find the strength she is seeking, so she is determined to participate in the Agon. According to the rules, she needs a mentor. With no identity or status, she faces repeated setbacks until she finally finds Cato as her "lifeline." The girl continues to hone her skills, passing the entry trials Cato set for her, and finally makes her first step into the Agon.

The Great Agon draws close as time passes. Besides a mentor, Augusta also needs a sponsor to participate in the Gladiatorial events. Sponsors are mostly nobles and merchants, and for someone with no identity or status, the only place to approach them is the underground arena, where nameless Gladiators are sold like commodities. Realizing she's become the bottom pick, Augusta takes the initiative by offering herself to the nobles and merchants in the audience, only to be met with waves of mockery. An old-school nobleman studies Augusta and offers her a deal: if Augusta manages to pass the three trials he sets, he will become her sponsor.

It is the day of the final trial, and the stands are filled with spectators. Everyone is eager to witness how a human will rival the strength of Arsinosa. Augusta looks up as Arsinosa appears. Facing the massive guardian of Septimont, she is unsure when the battle will begin. The moment Arsinosa opens her eyes, she immediately charges towards Augusta, who barely manages to deflect the attack even with her trained reflexes. After several exchanges, Augusta seizes an opportunity to land a strike on Arsinosa, but she is almost at her limit. To Augusta's surprise, Arsinosa halts its attack and bows. The audience erupts with thunderous applause, and the girl is raised to the high platform amidst the cheers. Only then does she realize that after gaining Arsinosa's approval, the people of Septimont will make a special exception for her. Augusta will bypass the Great Agon and be crowned "Champion."

Nestor has told you everything he knows, yet his stories barely scratch the surface of Augusta's life. In the end, Nestor poses his questions: What is it that has lifted Augusta to the seat of power? What is it that makes a ruler? He expects no quick answers, but hopes you will meet Augusta with these questions in mind and seek the answers yourself.

The Ephor's Palace rings with the Senators' criticisms toward Priestess Iuno as usual. After addressing their complaints, Augusta meets with the center of the grievances herself on the Palace roof. Iuno has some reservations about the upcoming hunting operation and their plans due to the prophecy she saw, but Augusta assures her firmly that she will fight to the very end.

==Glossary==
* Sanguis Plateaus - The Sanguis Plateaus were once the Septimont frontline against the Dark Tide. Due to the region's unique landscape, Remnant energy gathers here in unusual density, along with a Blightcloud perpetually looming overhead, formed since the first Dark Tide. During High Tide seasons, Gladiators from across Septimont arrive here to hunt Dark Tide creations in the name of glory.

* Lillibet - The current Head Priestess of Septimont.

* Book of Prophecies - A scroll Lillibet carries, recording visions glimpsed in the flame light. Both this book and the murals within Tetragon Temple are media through which the Priestesses of Septimont convey prophecies to the people.

* Hero of Heroes - The legendary ruler of Septimont. The legend traces its roots to an ancient prophecy that only the one who becomes the Hero of Heroes can save Septimont from falling into ruin.
